aic_unavailable: The Art Institute is not responding. Retrying shortly.
image_unavailable: That image could not be loaded. Trying another.
no_matching_artwork: Nothing in the index matches those filters.
too_many_requests: Taking a short break. The next artwork follows shortly.
attribution_with_description: Digital image courtesy of the Art Institute of Chicago. Description: Art Institute of Chicago, CC BY 4.0.
ai_disclaimer: AI-generated from the museum's metadata. Not a curatorial text.
ai_budget_exhausted: The interpretation budget for today is spent.
ai_key_none: No key saved. Interpretation is off.
ai_key_environment: Using the {provider} key from .env. Remove it there to change it.
ai_key_saved: Key saved. Press I on an artwork to read an interpretation.
ai_key_invalid: That cannot be an API key — check for spaces or a partial paste.
ai_key_failed: The key could not be saved.
ai_key_explainer: You type it here once, and vitrine sends it to the provider on your behalf. It is never sent back to this page, never written to a log, and everywhere else it appears it is cut down to its last four characters.
ai_storage_keyring: It is kept in your computer's own password store — Keychain on a Mac, Credential Manager on Windows. That is the safer of the two places it can go.
ai_storage_database: There is no password store available here, so the key sits unencrypted in vitrine's own file, data/vitrine.db. Anyone who can read that file can read the key, so do not copy or publish it. Installing the keyring extra moves the key into your computer's password store instead.
key_store_unavailable: Your system keyring refused to store the key.
panel_hint: Esc to close. Rotation is paused while this is open.
filters_no_index: No local index yet — run scripts/build_index.py to enable filters.
filters_too_thin: Nothing in the index has {minimum} or more artworks behind it yet.
hidden: Hidden. You will not see this one again.
mode_personal_hint: Built from what you have liked
mode_personal_hint_cold: {likes} of {minimum} favourites so far. Until then, Curated picks.
scoring_explain_intro: Curated ranks every indexed artwork by a weighted score over a few signals, all of them real fields from the museum's own data.
scoring_explain_caveat: These are our heuristics about what suits a screen, not claims about art.
scoring_is_boosted: The museum flagged it as an essential
scoring_resolution: Big enough to fill a large screen
scoring_metadata_completeness: Enough facts to caption it properly
scoring_has_alt_text: The museum wrote a visual description
scoring_artwork_type: The kind of object that fills a frame
mode_personal_cold: Showing Curated picks until you have liked a few more.
history_unavailable: That artwork is no longer available.
chrome_hidden: Just the artwork. Click again to bring the details back.
presets_empty: Nothing saved yet. Choose some filters and give them a name.
presets_applied_stale: Showing “{name}”. {count} of its filters are no longer in the index, so it may match less than it did.
presets_limit: That is as many saved filters as vitrine keeps. Remove one first.
filter_state_hint: Click to include, again to exclude, again to clear.
ambient_on_fullscreen: Fullscreen. The screen will stay awake.
filter_state_hint_include_only: Click to include, again to clear.
museum_aic_hint: Indexed locally. Every mode and filter.
museum_cma_hint: Fetched live. Random only, one filter.
mode_needs_index: Curated and For you rank against the local index, so they are only available for the Art Institute.
attribution_aic: Digital image courtesy of the Art Institute of Chicago.
attribution_cma: Digital image courtesy of the Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0.
access_not_describable: The museum has not written a visual description of this one, so there is nothing to build a description from.
access_slowed: Artworks will now change every {minutes} minutes, so there is time to listen.
access_grounded_alt: Written from the museum's own description of the image. No AI has seen the artwork itself.
access_grounded_description: Written from the museum's catalogue text. No AI has seen the artwork itself.
help_history: Back and forward through what you have seen
help_overlay: Pin or unpin the details, and ask for an interpretation
help_hold: Keep this artwork up five minutes longer
hold_limit: Held for an hour. That is the limit.
help_click: In fullscreen, hide or show everything but the artwork
help_escape: Close settings, then the details, then fullscreen
